blocks.x: A no-theater description of Lakehouse Architecture & Migration: what ships first, what it touches at operational stores, how it is verified, and the per workflow metric we commit to moving against baseline.
Lakehouse Architecture & Migration exists because the hard part of this work is not the model — it is the measurement, the ownership and the audit trail. That is what this page describes.

blocks.title: Governed lakehouse pipeline — Lakehouse Architecture & Migration
blocks.note: The flow is linear on purpose: every hop owns its latency budget and failure policy, and a regression in one stage is a cohort, never an estate-wide surprise.

blocks.x: What holds Lakehouse Architecture & Migration together is discipline at the boundaries — typed contracts between stages, versioned releases, and a replay trail for every decision. The diagram above shows how the pieces compose; the gate reviews are what keep them honest.

The build sequence is deliberate: contracts and identity first, the working decision slice second, the verification harness third — because a Lakehouse Architecture & Migration capability without its eval gate is just another unattended automation.

blocks.title: Delivery cadence — Lakehouse Architecture & Migration
blocks.note: Each gate reviews the measured delta against the signed baseline with the owners in the room; the calendar does the enforcing.
